thread:
Marie Chen: Heads up — customer ACME reporting intermittent 401s on signed callback endpoints since their deploy ~03:12 UTC. Failing signature verification: "no matching JWK kid" in our logs. Seen ~10% of requests fail, rest OK.
Alex Ruiz: Any repro curl or request id we can pass to them? Is this confined to a region?
Marie Chen: Only in us-west-2 so far. Customer provided a sample request-id: req_87a9c. Snippet from our verifier: 
```
verify_signature: error: signature verification failed: no matching key for kid=4f2b9c
jwks_fetch: 200 OK (cached)
jwks_etag: "b3f9a"
```
Jordan (support): Customer says they rotated keys earlier today and their IdP returned a new jwks endpoint immediately, but our side still returned the old keys for a while. They bumped their side back and problems reduced. Workaround we gave: ask them to retry + rotate again.
Isaac Ng: Could be JWKS cache staleness + upstream CDN caching. Our jwks cache uses Cache-Control max-age and ETag currently. If their IdP returns inconsistent headers during rotation, we can serve stale key sets and fail verification. Also clock skew could be compounding it (kid reused while token iat/exp slightly off).
Olivia Patel: I pulled a couple of failing token headers — iat and exp look fine but server time on verifier shows ~2.5m ahead of IdP's reported time (clockstep ~150s). We currently have leeway=60s in jwt verify. That won't cover >120s.
Isaac Ng: Repro steps I used locally:
```
# simulate rotated jwks served with old cache
python -m http.server 8000 &
# swap in old jwks.json then new jwks.json
curl -H "Accept: application/json" http://localhost:8000/.well-known/jwks.json
# run verifier against token with kid=old_kid
./bin/verifier --token-file bad-token.jwt --jwks-url http://localhost:8000/.well-known/jwks.json
```
Got same "no matching key" until I forced a cache refresh.
Marie Chen: Can we add a temporary mitigation: reduce JWKS TTL on fetcher to 30s and treat 5xx as don't-stale-reuse? Also bump leeway to 180s for signed callbacks route only?
Isaac Ng: I can push a patch to the jwks client: respect Cache-Control but cap max-age at 30s, implement background revalidate (stale-while-revalidate) with jitter, and add an opt-in route-specific leeway config. Minimal changes first: cap TTL + expose per-route leeway.
Olivia Patel: Also add telemetry: log when we fall back to stale keys + include ETag/age and server time vs token iat in trace. That will help customers and debugging.
sre-bot: Deploy started: jwks-cache-cap-30s -> staging (build 0.23.7).
Jordan (support): Customer accepted mitigation and testing. They asked for ETA. Can we give them an interim workaround?
Alex Ruiz: Interim: ask customer to reissue tokens after rotation and avoid immediate back-to-back rotates; we can also provide them a signed nonce challenge to force key fetch on our side. Not ideal but practical.
Marie Chen: Patch merged to staging. Isaac will run canary in us-west-2 for 1h. If green, deploy to prod and notify support.
Isaac Ng: Canary started at 2912345679. Observed initial successes — failing rate dropped from ~10% to <0.5% in the canary group.
Marie Chen: Customer confirmed reduced errors after we flipped the canary and set leeway for their tenant. They see 200s for callbacks again. :thumbsup:
Olivia Patel: Follow-ups: 1) postmortem writeup, 2) add tests simulating inconsistent jwks headers, 3) consider exposing a customer-facing TTL override for enterprise IdPs.
Jordan (support): Filing ticket INC-4521 with customer notes and mitigation timeline. Customer thanked us.
Marie Chen: Nice work. We'll ship the prod patch today and follow up in #incidents if anything else pops up. :party:
